PastHelp.veteran: A partial success finds a comrade in ports larger than a village; isolated places require full success. A comrade gives reliable information and may lend muscle in a major port. Refusing a favor strains the relationship.
PastHelp.seeker: You have scholarly contacts, access to closed libraries, and leads on contracts. Envious rivals start a new scheme once the last one is resolved.
PastHelp.colonist: You know the supply markets. Check for discounts on each deal, foraging at sea once per watch, and urban trouble at most once per session.
PastHelp.deprived: You have merchant aristocracy connections and start with five times the usual money. Choose two troubles; mark fragility if it is one of them.
PastHelp.savage: You know wildlife and field medicine. +2 advantages when hunting, +2 complications in social checks; medic is your only specialty. Forage on wild islands once per watch.
PastHelp.reconstructed: You know law, etiquette, and the underworld. You have an advantage when persuading or deceiving under pressure. A direct order from an official must be obeyed or you lose consciousness. Check for customs and former accomplices separately in each port.
PastHelp.remnant: Start with 3 luck marks (record manually). Unrest grows twice as fast and social collisions gain one complication. You witness an accident in each port.
PastHelp.augur: A divination check yields vague information. Start with no luck marks and gain none; unrest grows twice as fast. Discuss sacrifices and consequences with the group.
PastHelp.gambler: You have an advantage when gambling or escaping. You never back out of an accepted wager. Check for old debt connections at the port's finest den.
PastHelp.champion: Check for former glory in negotiations, and for challengers and admirers at social events. Without a massage every five watches, add one complication. Winning a contest inflicts a wound.
PastHelp.writer: +2 advantages when tailing, infiltrating, gathering information, or writing persuasively. Check for inspections in every port and for trouble after going out.
PastHelp.artist: You have an advantage when resolving social conflict peacefully; the second wound is fatal. Check for a fan once per scene, for rivals in port, and for critics in art venues.
PastHelp.hard_worker: +2d6 when respectfully negotiating with superiors; +1 complication in intellectual, legal or financial matters, or when being persistent or witty. No discounts. Only navigator or mechanic; the fourth wound is fatal.
PastHelp.sleeper: After being wounded, you can gain +20 advantages until the scene ends (at most one watch), then take another wound. Only one Sleeper per crew. If the ship leaves without you, the character is lost.
PastHelp.defect: You have an advantage in squad tactics and with military equipment. Check for old contacts at military sites in Olm Nde. Refusing an old debt costs you the contact.
PastHelp.slave: +2 advantages reading intentions, disguising yourself, moving things unseen, or adapting to a hierarchy. +2 complications showing strength or confidence. You cannot be captain and start with no savings.

Condition.LuckHelp: Spend one mark to guarantee success or prevent a wound. Record the effect manually.

Bargain.Title: Dramatic bargain
Bargain.Price: Agree on the goal, stakes and risks with the group. A dramatic bargain replaces the roll: partial success costs 1 point, full success costs 2. In the Roll20 reference rules, each complication adds 2 points, and each set of 4 advantages cancels one complication.
Bargain.Payment: For each point, spend 12 advantages, take an octad to prepare, add 8 unrest, or pay 3,000 og. multiplied by the representative's total number of merits and flaws. You can combine payments. Unrest gained this way cannot be reduced before the collision ends.
Bargain.Consequences: The group may also negotiate debt or a change in relationships: gaining a new enemy covers 3 points; losing a valued ally covers 4. If you accept the consequences instead of contesting them, each affected protagonist gains one luck mark.
